transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today? Is there something specific you'd like to talk about or any concerns you have?

Well, doctor, I... I suppose I'm here because I just keep losing these massive chunks of time, and it's getting to the point where it's really interfering with my day. I work with computers, you know, so I'm at a screen all day, and lately—well, maybe longer than lately—I just find myself getting completely stuck. 

I'll write an email, or even just a simple text message, and I have to re-read it. And I don't mean just glancing over it once to check for a typo, I mean reading it over and over and over again. And it's not just messages, either. I'll close a directory or a file folder on my desktop, and then I have this overwhelming urge to reopen it just to make absolutely sure I didn't accidentally delete something crucial or drag a file into the wrong place. 

And it happens before I leave the house, too, or right before I finally sit down to start my work. I'll just stand there, mentally replaying conversations I had the day before, word for word, going through every little detail and analyzing my tone and what the other person said. It's like... it's like I have to prove to myself, beyond a shadow of a doubt, that I didn't make some terrible, serious mistake. If I don't trace back every single step and verify it all in my head, I just can't move on to the next thing. And then suddenly forty-five minutes or an hour has gone by, and I haven't even started my morning. It's just exhausting, honestly, and I don't know how to stop doing it.
Do you ever have thoughts that pop into your mind that you don’t want or that upset you, like images or impulses that feel foreign to you?

Well, yes, actually. It’s exactly like that, just these thoughts that barge right in when I’m right in the middle of something else. I’ll be sitting at my desk—maybe I’m trying to work through a new system design, looking at the architecture, or even just preparing a lesson plan for this little coding workshop I run on the weekends—and out of nowhere, this thought just hits me. It’s this intense, nagging idea that I might have sent the wrong message to my ex-wife. Or that I somehow mishandled these old digital family photos we were supposed to split up, like maybe I deleted her copies or sent them to the wrong person entirely. 

And it’s not just about her, either. Sometimes it’s this sudden, heavy feeling that I’ve let someone in the community down, like I promised to fix a neighbor’s laptop and totally forgot, even though I haven't spoken to them in weeks. The thoughts just pop up, and they are so upsetting because I know, logically, that I’ve already been over this. I know I didn't send a bad text. I know the photos are safely backed up on three different drives. But the thought just sits there, and I can’t seem to let it pass. I try to push it away, I try to focus on the code on my screen, but it’s like a splinter in my brain. It just throbs and throbs until I have to stop everything and mentally retrace every single interaction I've had just to prove to myself that the thought isn't true. It's so frustrating because it has nothing to do with what I actually want to be thinking about.
